# Placement gate false-positive blocks epic driving on a busy machine

## Problem statement

`implement.py parent <epic>` refuses to proceed for an epic child whose
worktree exists but holds no changes whenever **any** other registered
worktree of the repository is dirty:

```
ERROR: Child WL-... produced changes in the sibling worktree
.../worktrees/wl-WL-0MVOA0XVC... instead of its worktree ...
Offending paths: ...
```

`_child_main_checkout_violation` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`)
treats "child worktree clean + sibling worktree dirty" as evidence that the
child wrote outside its tree. Condition 3 of its documented precision rule
says pre-existing/unrelated dirt must not block a legitimate child, but the
code only earns that exemption when the child's own worktree already holds
changes — which a **freshly started child never does**. The result: on a
machine running several concurrent dispatches (the normal steady state),
`parent` and `drive` fail closed before the first child session is ever
spawned.

## Evidence (captured 2026-11-18, parent epic WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9)

1. `implement.py parent WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9` started child
   WL-0MWKY141H002LULI and created its (empty) worktree.
2. `implement.py drive WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9` then failed in `phase_parent`
   with one message per dirty sibling worktree:
   - `wl-WL-0MVOA0XVC0002PBG-...` (item soft-deleted, 3 dirty paths)
   - `wl-WL-0MVOBP8MC0093Y7T-...` (blocked item, 22 dirty paths)
   - `wl-WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV-...` (live concurrent dispatch, 15 dirty paths)
   - `wl-WL-0MWMGEL5R003IH71-...` (6 dirty paths)
   - `/tmp/wl-base-check`, `/tmp/wl-clean-check`, ... (1 dirty path each)
   `sessions_spawned: 0` — no child session ran, so no child work existed.
3. Removing the empty worktree (`implement.py abort`) and re-running `drive`
   let the chain start normally: `phase_start` recreated the tree and the
   session was spawned, precisely because no clean worktree existed at the
   moment the placement check ran.

## Desired change

A freshly started child (worktree created, no session spawned against it yet)
must never be reported as a placement violation because of dirt in a
*different* work item's worktree. Candidate treatments, in order of
preference:

- Exempt a child whose worktree was created by this run's `phase_start` and
  has never had a session spawned against it (the same shape as the existing
  `read_spawn_failure` exemption).
- Restrict the sibling scan to worktrees whose dirt this child's session could
  have produced (age ordering vs the child worktree creation time).
- At minimum, fail-open (WARNING) when the offending sibling belongs to an
  independently live, non-terminal item (a concurrent dispatch), keeping the
  hard failure only for siblings whose item is terminal (deleted/completed),
  where the dirt genuinely is orphaned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A unit test drives `phase_parent`/`_child_main_checkout_violation` with a
  clean child worktree and at least one dirty sibling worktree owned by a
  distinct non-terminal item and asserts the child is reported startable, not
  failed.
- A second test pins the genuine case that must stay fail-closed: dirt in a
  sibling worktree attributable to this child's own session still fails
  placement.
- `implement.py drive <epic>` completes its first `parent` step and spawns the
  first child session on a repository where other items' worktrees are dirty.
- No existing placement/attribution test regresses.

## Impact

An epic can be driven on a machine that is also running other dispatches,
instead of the driver dead-ending before the first child session.

Discovered from WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 (deps: discovered-from:WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9).


## Related work

- WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 — parent epic from which this bug was discovered (discovered-from).
- WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG — completed guard work on `implement.py finish` wiping the main checkout; same placement/attribution area, no AC overlap.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_child_main_checkout_violation` (~L19973) holds the precision rule (condition 1–3) and the sibling-worktree scan; call sites in `phase_parent`/`phase_drive` (~L15684, ~L15745).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` — existing stray-write and spawn-failure coverage (`TestDrivenChildStraysIntoSiblingWorktree`, `TestSpawnFailureEvidence`, `TestSpawnFailedChildIsStartableAgain`).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_worktree_has_changes.py` — `_git_path_has_changes`/dirty-path helpers used by the guard.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MLYIK4AA1WJPZNU** – wl next Phase 4 should respect parent-child hierarchy when selecting among open items (completed)
- **WL-0MQF3H65W003ZGAS** – wl next should show parent instead of descending into child items (completed)
- **WL-0MQF95NCC0024H61** – wl next Stage 3 blocker surfacing still returns child items (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: abort, acceptance, age, already, also (+163 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: abort, acceptance, age, already, also (+158 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: abort, age, already, also, attribution (+129 more)

# Validate post-fix dispatch fairness after three days

Earliest run: **2026-11-22T15:30:00Z** (three days after the operator restarted
the downtime dispatcher panes on 2026-11-19T~15:15Z). Until that instant there
is no post-fix window long enough to judge, so this item is scheduled with
`startOn` rather than being dispatched immediately.

Follow-up from **WL-0MWKY1KL8009PS7K** (the post-fix re-measurement, which was
reported *inconclusive* because the live dispatcher was still running pre-fix
code) and from parent **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** AC5.

## Why

The fairness fix (whole-set round-robin rotation + `RUN_LENGTH_CEILING = 2`,
commits `ef46c0bd8` / `7a0d1460c`) is now live: the operator restarted every
Herdr `Work Items` plugin pane, so the dispatcher loads current
`packages/herdr/src`. The only remaining question is whether the live
behaviour actually meets the thresholds over a real window — which needs
elapsed time, not code.

## Users

The operator of the multi-project Herdr workspace (single user, 10 registered
project roots), who relies on the downtime dispatcher to spread agent sessions
evenly instead of letting one project monopolise the slots.

- As the workspace operator, I want a measured pass/fail on the fairness rule
  over a real post-restart window, so that "the fix works" is evidence rather
  than assumption.
- As the workspace operator, I want the measurement reproducible from the logs
  alone, so that a future reader can re-derive it after the logs have rotated.

## Scope

Read-only validation. No code change is expected; if the numbers fail, record
the evidence and file a follow-up work item rather than editing the dispatcher
from this item.

- Confirm from `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` that decision entries now
  carry the fairness metric (`selectedRoot`, and `dispatchingRoot` +
  `consecutiveRunLength` on consumed dispatches) — proof the current code is
  live.
- Measure the window from each project's `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`
  (rows with a `paneId`) using the counting rules recorded in
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- Cross-check the dispatch-log distribution against the decision-log fairness
  metric (the accounting identity).
- Report the result on **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9**.

## Existing state

Captured at intake (2026-11-19T23:35Z) — indicative only; it is **not** the
measurement this item asks for, and the measured window must still be taken
after 2026-11-22T15:30Z.

- **The regime check already passes by observation.** Fairness-bearing decision
  entries (`selectedRoot`) first appear at `2026-11-19T18:01:53.039Z`
  (`projects/tce-the-rising/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`) and, in the
  downtime leader's own log, from `2026-11-19T20:47:02.017Z`
  (`projects/SorraAgents/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`) — both after the
  ~15:15Z restart, so the running code includes the fairness accounting. AC1
  should be re-confirmed against the measured window, not assumed from this.
- The leader's log is where decisions land: 17 fairness-bearing decision rows
  between `2026-11-19T20:47:02Z` and `2026-11-19T23:34:39Z` — 14
  `reason: "dispatched"`, 3 `reason: "reservation-refused"`. Distinct
  `selectedRoot`s: SorraAgents 5, ContextHub 5, AI_Hell 3, tce-the-rising 2,
  games_curator 2 (5 active projects ≥ the three-project floor).
- Every recorded `consecutiveRunLength` in that leader-log window is `1`; the
  only `2` observed today is `2026-11-19T18:17:34.785Z` in
  `projects/tce-the-rising/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`. 14 dispatches is
  far too small a sample to declare anything.
- **Open point for the measurement:** 2 of the 17 rows record `selectedRoot`
  ≠ `dispatchingRoot` (`18:01:53Z` and `23:18:07Z`). The counting rules charge
  `dispatchingRoot`, so this is either a benign deferral/ordering effect or a
  real accounting-identity mismatch — the AC4 cross-check is where it gets
  settled, and the finding must be stated either way.
- The round-robin cursor file (`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`)
  currently lists 10 roots; the recent window served 5 of them.

## Data sources (read-only)

- `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` — per project; the leader's copy carries
  the decision rows (periodically rotated, ~500 lines).
- `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` — per project; dispatch rows carrying a
  `paneId` (rotated, ~500 lines per project — evidence disappears within
  hours, so capture aggregates as soon as they are read).
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json` — cursor state at the
  window boundary.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — the counting rules ("*Counting rules.*"
  section: window, rows, project key, regime check, even share, consecutive
  run, kind mix, accounting identity).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A decision entry carrying `selectedRoot` is observed after the restart
  timestamp, confirming the current code is live.
- A window with at least three active projects is measured, stating the window
  (UTC start/end), the project count and the counting rules used.
- No project exceeds twice its even share of dispatches in that window, and no
  project holds a consecutive run longer than 2.
- The distribution derived from the decision-log fairness metric agrees with
  the dispatch-log aggregates for the same window.
- The table (per-project counts, longest consecutive runs, kind mix) and an
  explicit pass/fail against both thresholds are reported on
  WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9; a fail records the evidence, the suspected cause and a
  follow-up work item.
- If the window has fewer than three active projects, the measurement is
  recorded as inconclusive (with the extended window or the reason it could
  not be extended) rather than declared a pass.
- The captured aggregates and the exact read-only commands/queries used are
  recorded on this work item (not only in the report comment), so the result
  can be re-derived after the logs rotate.
- Any documentation claim that the measurement contradicts (e.g. in
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`) is corrected; if that — or a follow-up fix
  arising from a fail — produces a code or doc change, the full project test
  suite must pass with that change.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Read-only: no dispatcher behaviour change, no gate change, no scheduler
  change.
- Measure only after the restart marker is visible — a window spanning the
  restart would mix two code versions.
- Log rotation (500 lines per project) discards evidence within hours: capture
  the aggregates as soon as they are read and record them on the item.
- Report on a completed parent (**WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9**, `completed`/`in_review`)
  via a comment; do not reopen it.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Small sample.** Rotation keeps ~500 lines per project and the recent rate is
  ~14 dispatches in 3 hours, so a three-day window may still be a thin sample;
  state the dispatch total and do not declare a pass on a handful of rows.
- **Too few active projects.** Overnight/weekend windows can drop below three
  active projects; AC6 already requires recording *inconclusive* rather than a
  pass.
- **Mixed regime.** Any window reaching back past `2026-11-19T18:01Z` mixes the
  pre-fix worker's rows; the window must start after the restart marker.
- **Assumption:** the leader's `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` (currently
  SorraAgents) is the canonical decision log; per-project logs receive only the
  rows that project's pane produced.
- **Assumption:** `dispatchingRoot` is the charged root (the counting rules say
  so), so the two observed `selectedRoot` ≠ `dispatchingRoot` rows are explained
  by deferral/ordering rather than by a defect — AC4 must prove it.
- **Scope-creep risk.** A failing measurement invites an immediate dispatcher
  fix; that is deliberately out of scope here (read-only), so any fix becomes a
  new linked work item with its own ACs and release gate.

## Impact

The operator gets a measured, reproducible verdict on whether the dispatcher's
fixed fair-sharing actually holds live, so even distribution across their
projects is evidenced rather than assumed.

**Key Files:**

- `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` (per project; read-only) — decision rows; regime check (`selectedRoot`) and accounting identity (`dispatchingRoot`, `consecutiveRunLength`)
- `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (per project; read-only) — dispatch rows with a `paneId`; per-project counts, runs, kind mix
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json` — cursor state at the window boundary
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — counting rules and thresholds to quote with the result
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-coordination.ts` — where the fairness fields are written (reference only; no change expected)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-entries.ts` — dispatch-row shape (`paneId`, `cwd`, `kind`)

## Related work

- **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** — *Dispatcher seems to unevenly distribute work*
  (completed/in_review) — the epic; AC5 is this validation, and the report goes
  here.
- **WL-0MWKY1KL8009PS7K** — *Re-measure dispatch concentration after the fix*
  (completed/in_review) — the first attempt; reported *inconclusive* because
  the live worker still ran pre-fix code. Its counting methodology and outcome
  section are the template for this item.
- **WL-0MWKY141H002LULI** — *Record per-project fairness metric on dispatch
  decisions* (completed) — added the `selectedRoot`/`dispatchingRoot`/
  `consecutiveRunLength` fields this measurement reads.
- **WL-0MWKY1GK4001IFUD** — *Docs: the enforced fair-scheduling rule and its
  metric* (completed) — the counting rules and metric documentation.
- **WL-0MWKY1839000JM5O** — *Rotate the whole admissible candidate set with a
  run-length bound* (completed) — the fix under test (`RUN_LENGTH_CEILING = 2`).
- **WL-0MWO38U4W002853V** — *Publish fairness report and update documentation*
  (blocked/intake_complete) — downstream consumer of a passing result; blocked,
  so it cannot absorb this measurement.
- Repo docs: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — "Re-measuring concentration
  after a fix" / *Counting rules*.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No interview questions were asked.** The item had been re-scoped by a prior
  `implement` session and already carried a problem statement, scope, six
  testable acceptance criteria, data sources and constraints, so the interview
  was skipped per the intake contract (seed context sufficient to draft).
- **Q: Is this a duplicate of the completed re-measurement (WL-0MWKY1KL8009PS7K)?**
  — Answer (agent research, source: `wl show WL-0MWKY1KL8009PS7K --json`): No.
  That item closed *inconclusive* because the live dispatcher still ran pre-fix
  code; its ACs were therefore not satisfied by observation. This item measures
  a fresh window after the operator's restart, which is the gap it leaves.
  Partial overlap only — no rewrite needed; the description already isolates the
  post-restart window.
- **Q: Is `chore` the right issue type?** — Answer (agent decision): yes — no
  code behaviour changes; this is operational validation plus reporting, with a
  conditional doc correction only on a contradictory finding.
- **Q: Why was the automated `/skill:find-related` report not generated?** —
  Answer (agent research): the script re-claims the item with
  `--status in-progress`, which the `startOn` claim guard
  (`src/claim-start-on.ts`, WL-0MWMGEUT10056MUI) refuses with
  `start_on_not_reached` until 2026-11-22T15:30Z, and it exposes no
  `--force-start-on` passthrough. The `## Related work` list above was therefore
  gathered manually from `wl search` / `wl list --parent` and is idempotent to
  re-run later.

## Outcome (measured 2026-11-23T10:12Z)

**Concentration PASS, run-length FAIL.** Window `2026-11-22T15:30:00Z` →
`2026-11-23T10:10:00Z`, 53 dispatches, 5 active projects, even share 10.6,
largest project SorraAgents 16 = **1.51×** (below the 2× ceiling). Longest
consecutive run = **3**, twice (SorraAgents 2026-11-22T21:02Z→21:35Z;
Tableau-Card-Engine 2026-11-23T00:46Z→00:58Z) against a ceiling of 2 → the
run-length threshold is **not met**.

- **Regime check: PASS.** Leader instance (TCE workspace, root
  `Tableau-Card-Engine`) started 2026-11-19T15:16:24Z; 655 fairness-bearing
  decision rows retained from 2026-11-23T02:44:57Z, including 13
  `outcome: "dispatched"` rows with `selectedRoot` + `dispatchingRoot` +
  `consecutiveRunLength`.
- **Accounting identity: exact where evidence survives.** On 03:17Z→10:07Z
  (13 dispatches) per-project `dispatchingRoot` counts and the maximum
  `consecutiveRunLength` (2) reproduce the dispatch-log aggregates exactly; the
  earlier 40 dispatches have no decision-log counterpart because the leader's
  500-line log rotates ≈ every 2.2 h, so their runs' precondition cannot be
  re-derived.
- **Open point settled.** `selectedRoot` ≠ `dispatchingRoot` is benign: the
  `selectedRoot` is pinned to `tce-the-rising` (never charged while its offer was
  never consumed) and the leader falls through to the next least-recently-served
  root — the whole-set rotation working, with `dispatchingRoot` as the accounting
  key.
- **Reported** on WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 (comment `WL-C0MWT402WL00415QJ`) with the
  table, kind mix, both threshold verdicts and the suspected causes.
- **Follow-up:** **WL-0MWT3Z9M9002Z9BF** (discovered-from this item) —
  leadership-independent, auditable run-length accounting plus the counting-rule
  precondition.
- **Docs:** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` records this measurement and states
  the run-length threshold with its precondition.

# Allow 2x implement/audit budget while panes wait for a model to be re-enabled

## User story

As an operator, when an implement or audit pane is stuck waiting for a model/provider to be re-enabled, I want the dispatcher to keep the local LLM slots earning by admitting extra implement/audit work, up to double the configured budget, instead of idling at the normal cap.

## Background

`model-cooldowns.json` is the machine-wide signal that a pane is blocked on a throttled provider (`cooldownUntil > now`); the stalled-work scan already treats an active entry as "never wake early" and a due entry as a wake trigger (WL-0MV5639GG00085Q7). The host-budget dispatcher nevertheless counts those panes as live and refuses new work at the configured cap (`maxImplement`, `maxAudit`), even though the blocked panes cannot use the model.

The 2026-11-22/23 overnight run showed the cost: 14 agent sessions open (5 implement, 5+ audit, 1 intake), 175 provider-exhaustion turns across 42 sessions, and several sessions 11-17 h old. The fleet idled at the configured caps while panes waited for the provider to come back.

## Detection

A pane is **model-blocked** when it has an active machine-wide model-cooldown entry (matched by `paneId` or `sessionId`) whose kind is `implement` or `audit` - kind from the entry when present, otherwise from the pane label. This is the canonical "waiting on a model to be re-enabled" signal.

If the implementation also consumes a proxy model-availability signal (model disabled/loading/switching), it must be documented and tested. Absent, unreadable or corrupt signals must **not** grant relief (fail closed).

## Relief rule

- While at least one model-blocked pane of a capped kind exists, that kind's admission cap is `min(2 x configured cap, hard ceiling)`, where the hard ceiling is **2x the configured cap** and cannot be raised by settings or env.
- The total live count (including the blocked panes) must not exceed the effective cap.
- Relief is **per kind**: a blocked implement raises only the implement cap; a blocked audit raises only the audit cap.
- Plan/intake/risk-effort remain uncapped and are not affected.
- Relief ends immediately when the last matching cooldown expires or is cleared: the cap returns to the configured value on the next admission read, with no restart and no stuck double cap.
- Relief only raises the host-budget cap; every other gate (free slots, prefill pacing, CPU, review-queue depth, producer review, attempt budget, code-freeze, audit freshness) is unchanged.

## Audit-arm dependency (must not be faked)

The proxy audit lease remains authoritative (`/llama/local/audit/availability`, `cap`, atomic `/llama/local/audit/lease`). herdr must never invent a second lease. If the proxy still grants `cap: 1`, an audit relief dispatch must still refuse `audit-budget-saturated`. The item must land one of:

- a coordinated proxy contract that grants a relief audit cap while an audit is model-blocked; or
- an explicit, documented scoping of the audit arm to the legacy local-budget mode (`HERDR_AUDIT_LOCAL_BUDGET=1`) with evidence, until the proxy supports relief.

The implement arm must not be blocked on the audit-arm dependency.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A documented, unit-tested model-blocked predicate: an active entry for an implement/audit pane -> blocked; expired/absent -> not blocked; corrupt/unreadable signal -> not blocked (fail closed); unknown kind -> not blocked; kind resolved from the pane label when the entry's kind is `null`.
2. `admitHostDispatch` computes `effectiveCap(kind) = min(configuredCap x 2, 2 x configuredCap)` while a model-blocked pane of that kind exists; otherwise `configuredCap`. Per-kind independence is pinned (blocked implement does not raise audit and vice versa).
3. The effective cap is a **total live** cap including the blocked panes; admission refuses above it with the normal budget token. No path can admit beyond the effective cap.
4. A clock-advance test proves relief ends when `cooldownUntil` passes and the cap reverts without a restart.
5. A corrupt/unreadable `model-cooldowns.json` (reader returns `null`) yields the normal cap, with decision evidence naming the unreadable signal.
6. Audit arm: a test proves herdr never invents a lease; with proxy `cap: 1` an audit relief dispatch remains `audit-budget-saturated`; the proxy contract change (or legacy-mode scoping) is recorded as a dependency with its own work item if required.
7. Both dispatcher paths (coordination leader `dispatchFromCoordination` and direct `dispatchDowntimeWork`) produce the same effective cap; a pin asserts there is no path that bypasses `admitHostDispatch`.
8. Table-driven proof that relief never relaxes any other gate (free slots, prefill cap/ETA, CPU, review-queue hold, producer review, attempt budget, code-freeze, audit freshness).
9. Decision-log evidence `budgetRelief: { kind, baseCap, effectiveCap, blockedPaneIds, reason, until }` is recorded on an admission with relief and on a refusal above the effective cap; a `budget-relief` header/decision token is added to the vocabulary; the worklist counter shows `n/effectiveCap`.
10. Kill switch `downtimeBudgetReliefEnabled` (default `true`) restores the configured cap when off; the multiplier is fixed at 2 and cannot be raised by settings or env.
11. Docs updated: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md`, `CONFIG.md`, and the model-cooldown contract header (`packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts`) notes the new consumer.
12. Changed-scope and full test suites green before `in_review`.

## Out of scope

- Raising the proxy's slot count or `max_audits` beyond the relief rule; the proxy remains the authority for audit leases.
- Auto-resuming or aborting model-blocked panes (that is the stalled-work wake path).
- Exceeding 2x under any circumstances.

## Related

- WL-0MV5639GG00085Q7 - bounded model-cooldown wake (machine-wide signal + stalled-work integration).
- WL-0MVXY0YG7009JMHI / WL-0MWAMSK9H005BOHD - host dispatch budget and proxy-derived audit admission.
- WL-0MWDDHVF2004PTYX - audit-budget refusal precedence and evidence.
- `~/.herdr/downtime/model-cooldowns.json` - the machine-wide signal.

## Impact

When a dispatched implement or audit is parked waiting for its model to come back, herdr can keep otherwise-idle local LLM slots earning by admitting additional implement/audit work up to double the normal cap, instead of idling at the configured budget.

## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-23)

Decomposition: 11 children in four vertical-slice phases, each cutting through module + tests + wiring + observability + docs; every phase is preceded by its test item (test-first ordering is enforced with dependency edges).

| Phase | Children | Slice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 — predicate and cap contract | Test: model-blocked predicate and relief cap (WL-0MWTASN6H0005KED) -> Implement: host-budget-relief predicate and cap (WL-0MWTASWOE0033YEH) | new pure module, unit suite, contract-of-record header |
| 2 — admission and surfaces | Test: relief admission across both dispatcher paths (WL-0MWTASOSV0004O6J) -> Implement: relief in admission and dispatcher (WL-0MWTASY9100813PD) -> Implement: relief evidence and budget counters (WL-0MWTASZNA008AQOK) | `admitHostDispatch` + both dispatcher paths + decision log + worklist header + skip line + interactive threshold |
| 3 — operator control and audit arm | Implement: downtimeBudgetReliefEnabled kill switch (WL-0MWTAT1O300673UQ), Test: audit lease authority under relief (WL-0MWTASQDU002HDYR) -> Implement: audit-arm relief scoping (WL-0MWTAT3090003CA6) | settings kill switch, lease-authority pin, legacy-mode scoping |
| 4 — regression, docs, verification | Test: relief relaxes no other gate (WL-0MWTASS0T0037XP6), Docs: budget relief contract (WL-0MWTAT4BP0055B8T) -> Verify: acceptance criteria and green suites (WL-0MWTAT65H009VPAQ) | non-relaxation matrix, four docs, AC evidence + green suites |

Decisions taken while planning (each is a documented assumption, reversible):

- **Fixed multiplier.** Relief is exactly 2x and lives as a module constant in `host-budget-relief.ts`; no setting, no `budget.json` key and no env var can raise it (parent AC10). `HOST_BUDGET_MAX = 32` continues to bound only the *configured* cap.
- **Audit arm (parent AC6, option 2).** Audit relief is scoped to the legacy local-budget mode (`HERDR_AUDIT_LOCAL_BUDGET=1`) with evidence, because the proxy lease is authoritative and herdr must never invent a second lease. No cross-repo work item is created; the proxy contract change is recorded as a documented dependency inside the audit-arm children. The implement arm is not blocked by it.
- **Interactive threshold.** The hand-fired over-quota dialog uses the same effective cap as admission, so the header (`5/10`) and the prompt cannot disagree. Human override above the effective cap is unchanged.
- **Signal.** `~/.herdr/downtime/model-cooldowns.json` is the only relief signal; no proxy model-availability (disabled/loading/switching) signal is consumed or inferred.
- **Fail direction.** An unreadable/corrupt cooldown read grants no relief (fail closed) and records evidence naming the unreadable signal — the opposite of the reader's own "assume active" convention, deliberately, so a corrupt file cannot inflate the host budget.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which of the two parent AC6 options should the audit arm land — a coordinated proxy contract that grants a relief audit cap, or scoping audit relief to the legacy local-budget mode?" — Answer (plan, from the item's own AC6 and the shipped admission contract): **legacy-mode scoping**, with the proxy lease remaining authoritative. Evidence: `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts` (two-step availability pre-check + atomic lease), `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §proxy-derived audit admission. **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking, producer may override):** if the producer prefers the coordinated proxy contract, the audit-arm children change and a proxy-repo item is required; the implement arm is unaffected.
- Q: "Should the fixed 2x multiplier be reachable from settings/env so an operator can tune it?" — Answer (plan, from parent AC10): no. Evidence: AC10 pins "the multiplier is fixed at 2 and cannot be raised by settings or env".
- Q: "Does relief need to consume a proxy model-availability signal (disabled/loading/switching)?" — Answer (plan, from the parent Detection section): no; the machine-wide cooldown file is the canonical signal, and any future proxy signal needs its own documented, tested change. Evidence: `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts` contract header, `~/.herdr/downtime/model-cooldowns.json` (3 active entries observed at planning time: audit, intake, implement).
- Q: "Should relief relax the interactive over-quota dialog threshold?" — Answer (plan): yes, to the same effective cap, so the counter and the prompt agree; the human-override path above the effective cap is unaffected. Evidence: `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts`.
- Research: duplicate-work detection — searched `wl` for "budget relief", "admitHostDispatch", "model-cooldown", "host dispatch budget", "maxImplement", "double budget", "2x budget", "model blocked". No open duplicate exists; the nearest completed predecessors are WL-0MWF34932000SNTX (generic admission), WL-0MWAMSK9H005BOHD (admission choke point) and WL-0MV5639GG00085Q7 (bounded cooldown wake). Result: no overlap requiring closure or rewrite.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-23 — plan skill: decomposed into 11 children (4 phases), wired 13 dependency edges (test before implementation in every phase), recorded the five planning decisions above, and recorded the Appendix. Pre-check: `plan-if-needed` returned `plan` (effort Large, risk High); approval gate returned `request_approval: false` (Extra Large + High risk not met). AC coverage review: 100% covered, `proceed`.

# Cross-repo dependency edges are silently dropped by the sync prefix filter

## Summary

A dependency edge whose target is a **foreign** (cross-project) work item id is
silently deleted during `wl sync`, so a recorded cross-repo blocker disappears
from the local store. The loss has **two** drop points — the merge-time prefix
filter and the store's destructive import edge guard — both of which must be
fixed for a cross-repo edge to survive a full or delta sync.

## Problem

A dependency edge whose target is a **foreign** (cross-project) work item id is
removed by the sync path, so a recorded cross-repo blocker can silently
disappear from the local store on a `wl sync`.

Discovered-from `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` (2026-11-26): recording the cross-repo
blocker `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` → `SA-0MWFFD9N0050SP5` (a `../SorraAgents` item)
with `wl dep add`, then running `wl sync`: the edge was present before the sync
and absent afterwards (`select … from dependency_edges where fromId=…` returned
no rows). A minimal reproduction is recorded in a comment on this item: the
store held two outbound edges — `→ SA-0MWFFD9N0050SP5` (foreign target) and
`→ WL-0MWXIT6H3006TY2I` (local target); after `wl sync` only the local-target
edge remained. Same condition, different outcome purely by target prefix.

## Users

The people and systems that must keep seeing a cross-repo block:

- **Producer / agent sequencing cross-repo work** — e.g. `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG`
  is blocked on this item and cannot reach `in_review` until a
  `../SorraAgents` item lands; its producer-chosen sequencing relies on the
  edge surviving sync.
- **`wl next`, the audit gates and the worklist** — must keep treating a
  cross-repo blocker as active until the foreign endpoint is resolved.

Example user stories:

- As a producer, I record `wl dep add <local> <foreign>` and expect the block
  to still be there after `wl sync`, so I can sequence work across repositories.
- As an agent running `wl next`, I expect an item blocked on a foreign item to
  stay blocked (and to be reported as such) instead of silently becoming
  eligible.

## Root cause

There are **two** drop points. Fixing only the first (the item's original
pointer) still fails the round-trip ACs.

1. **Merge-time prefix filter** — `src/sync/prefix-filter.ts:82`:

   ```ts
   const keptEdges = edges.filter(e => allowedItemIds.has(e.fromId) && allowedItemIds.has(e.toId));
   ```

   `allowedItemIds` contains only the ids of pulled items that match the local
   project prefix (`isOwnProjectItemId`). A cross-repo edge's target id is by
   definition never in that set, so every foreign-target edge arriving from the
   remote is filtered out of the merged edge set.

2. **Destructive import edge guard** — `packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts:227`
   (`importWorkItems`, used by the full-snapshot persist path in
   `src/commands/sync.ts` ≈ line 460):

   ```ts
   if (ctx.store.getWorkItem(edge.fromId) && ctx.store.getWorkItem(edge.toId)) {
     desiredEdges.set(`${edge.fromId}\u0000${edge.toId}`, edge);
   }
   ```

   `desiredEdges` only includes edges whose **both** endpoints resolve to a
   locally-stored work item. A `local → foreign` edge has no local row for the
   foreign target, so it is excluded from `desiredEdges`; the subsequent delete
   loop removes it from `dependency_edges`. The non-destructive delta path
   (`upsertItems`, ≈ line 329) has the same both-endpoints-local guard, so a
   *new* foreign edge arriving in a delta is not persisted (existing ones
   survive because upsert never deletes).

The merge itself (`mergeDependencyEdges` in `src/sync/merge-collateral.ts`) is a
**union** of local and remote edges and therefore preserves local foreign
edges; the loss happens downstream — on the remote side (prefix filter) and on
the persist side (endpoint guard). This also explains the repro's
"re-adding and syncing again kept it" observation: a delta persist
(`upsertItems`) never deletes, whereas a full persist (`import`) does (see
Appendix A2).

Foreign-edge support itself is intentional (`WL-0MVWEENZL008XGYC`, parent
`WL-0MVWABT2Z001XMSD`; `wl dep add --help`: "dependsOn may be a foreign
cross-project id"), and `src/cross-repo/foreign-store.ts` reads the sibling
store read-only to display such edges — so both guards contradict the feature.

## Impact

Recording a dependency on another project's work item now actually holds — the
block stays visible after a sync instead of quietly evaporating.

## Why it matters

- A cross-repo blocker (e.g. "this item cannot reach `in_review` until a
  sibling repository's item lands") is unenforceable: it vanishes on the next
  pull, and nothing reports the deletion.
- Silent relationship loss is data loss: `wl next`, the audit gates and the
  worklist all stop seeing the block with no diagnostic.
- `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` is directly affected — its producer-chosen sequencing
  (Q2 = C: record the `../SorraAgents` skill switch as a blocker) relies on the
  edge surviving sync.
- Every operator using cross-repo dependencies (documented in
  `MULTI_PROJECT_GUIDE.md`) silently loses their recorded blockers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `filterRemoteDataByPrefix` keeps an edge when **either** endpoint is an
  allowed local item (equivalently: drops only edges whose endpoints are both
  foreign), pinned to the `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` → `SA-0MWFFD9N0050SP5`
  regression case.
- The store's import/upsert edge guard persists an edge when **either** endpoint
  resolves to a stored work item, so a `local → foreign` edge survives a full
  (`importWorkItems`) and a delta (`upsertItems`) persist; an edge is dropped
  only when neither endpoint resolves to a stored item.
- A cross-repo edge survives a full sync round-trip: `wl dep add <local>
  <foreign>` → `wl sync` (full snapshot) → the edge is still present in
  `dependency_edges` and still reported by `wl dep list <local>`.
- A cross-repo edge survives a delta sync between an ahead and a behind store,
  and is never resurrected after the local item that owns it is deleted.
- Loss is never silent: if any edge must be dropped during a merge/persist,
  `wl sync` reports the count and the affected ids (same visibility as the
  existing `Foreign-prefix filter: dropped N remote item(s)` line).
- The JSONL export emits a `local → foreign` edge on the owning item's
  `dependencies` array (round-trip guard) and the import re-hydrates it.
- Existing behaviour for foreign **items** is unchanged: foreign items and their
  comments/audit results are still never imported.
- Tests cover: the filter's either-endpoint rule, the import/upsert
  either-endpoint rule, a full sync round-trip, a delta ahead/behind sync, the
  delete-then-stale-remote non-resurrection case, and the dropped-edge
  diagnostic.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Two-stage fix, not one.** The prefix filter alone does not satisfy the
  round-trip ACs; the destructive import endpoint guard must be relaxed in the
  same change (see Root cause).
- **Existing test asserts the bug.** `tests/sync-prefix-filter.test.ts:120`
  ("drops dependency edges that touch dropped foreign items") currently expects
  `GUA-001 → WL-001` to be dropped; that expectation must be inverted (only
  both-foreign edges now drop).
- **Foreign items must still be dropped.** The prefix filter is
  defense-in-depth against cross-project pollution (`SA-0MSC0BM1V0032UYT`);
  only *edges owned by a local item* may survive, never foreign items,
  comments or audits.
- **Filter discipline is non-negotiable.** No path may import a foreign *item*;
  the fix must not weaken `isOwnProjectItemId` or the repo-context guard.
- **Backwards compatibility.** Same-project edge behaviour and existing sync
  output must be unchanged; the new diagnostic is additive.
- **Scope creep guard.** Related opportunities discovered during the fix (e.g. a
  general dependency-edge tombstone for `dep rm` resurrection) are logged as
  separate work items linked from this one, not folded in (see Appendix A3).

## Existing state

- `filterRemoteDataByPrefix` (`src/sync/prefix-filter.ts`) returns
  `{ items, comments, edges, audits, droppedItems }`; edges require both
  endpoints to be allowed.
- `importWorkItems` (`packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts`) performs a
  destructive differential replace; edges require both endpoints to be locally
  stored, and edges absent from `desiredEdges` are deleted.
- `upsertItems` (same file) saves an edge only when one endpoint is in the
  upserted batch **and** both endpoints are locally stored.
- `sync.ts` logs `Foreign-prefix filter: dropped N remote item(s) …` when items
  are dropped, but reports nothing about dropped edges.
- JSONL export embeds edges inside work items via
  `dependenciesFromEdges(normalizedEdges, item.id)` (`src/jsonl.ts`), so a
  `local → foreign` edge is already emitted on the local item's
  `dependencies` array; a `foreign → local` edge is never emitted because the
  foreign item is not exported.
- `getAllDependencyEdges()` selects all edges with no prefix filter.

## Desired change

- `filterRemoteDataByPrefix`: `keptEdges` becomes
  `allowedItemIds.has(e.fromId) || allowedItemIds.has(e.toId)`, and the result
  gains `droppedEdges: string[]` (e.g. `"WL-A->SA-B"`).
- `src/commands/sync.ts`: log a `Foreign-prefix filter: dropped N edge(s) …`
  line alongside the existing dropped-item line, mirroring its human/JSON
  visibility.
- `importWorkItems` / `upsertItems`: the endpoint guard becomes
  `getWorkItem(fromId) || getWorkItem(toId)`; a deleted local owner therefore
  drops its edges (cascade) and cannot be resurrected by a stale remote
  snapshot.
- `src/jsonl.ts`: add a round-trip guard test (no behaviour change expected —
  confirm the export/import path already carries foreign-target edges).
- Tests and docs updated as listed in the ACs.

## Key Files

- `src/sync/prefix-filter.ts` — the either-endpoint rule, the `droppedEdges`
  diagnostic and unit tests.
- `packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts` — relax the both-endpoints-local
  guard in `importWorkItems` (≈ line 227) and `upsertItems` (≈ line 329).
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — surface the dropped-edge count alongside the
  existing dropped-item line (≈ line 267).
- `src/jsonl.ts` — round-trip guard for foreign-target edges on
  `dependenciesFromEdges` / `importFromJsonlContent`.
- `tests/sync-prefix-filter.test.ts` — invert the existing edge-drop
  expectation and add the `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` → `SA-0MWFFD9N0050SP5`
  regression case.
- `tests/database-transactional-import-next.test.ts` (or a new focused import
  test) — foreign-endpoint survival through `import`/`upsertItems`, delete then
  stale-remote non-resurrection.
- `tests/jsonl.test.ts` — export/import round-trip of a foreign-target edge.
- `MULTI_PROJECT_GUIDE.md` — note that cross-repo edges survive sync and that
  only fully-foreign edges are dropped (with the diagnostic).
- `docs/CROSS_PROJECT_POLLUTION_CLEANUP.md` — record that the merge-time prefix
  filter keeps local-owner foreign edges and reports dropped-edge ids.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — update the `src/sync/prefix-filter.ts` row if the
  contract changes.

## Test plan

- **Unit — filter:** `filterRemoteDataByPrefix` keeps `local→foreign` and
  `foreign→local`, drops `foreign→foreign`, and reports the dropped pairs.
- **Unit — persist:** `importWorkItems` and `upsertItems` keep an edge with one
  local endpoint and one foreign endpoint; drop an edge with both foreign; drop
  the edge when the local owner is deleted.
- **Integration — full sync round-trip:** real temp repo, `wl dep add` with a
  foreign id, `wl sync`, assert `dependency_edges` and `wl dep list` still show
  it (`tests/sync-prefix-filter.test.ts` CLI section or a new
  `tests/cli/sync-cross-repo-edge.test.ts`).
- **Integration — delta sync:** ahead/behind stores; a foreign edge added on
  the ahead store survives the delta merge; deleting the owner then syncing a
  stale behind store does not resurrect it.
- **Diagnostic:** a sync whose remote carries a fully-foreign edge logs the
  count and ids; a sync with none logs nothing new.
- **Regression:** existing same-project edge behaviour and the foreign
  item/comment/audit drops are unchanged.

## Related work

- `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` (**Add a table for ACs**, epic) — **blocked on this
  item**; it needs the cross-repo edge fix to sequence the `../SorraAgents`
  skill switch.
- `WL-0MVWEENZL008XGYC` (**Foreign dependency edge CRUD**) — the intentional
  feature this filter contradicts; foreign ids are supported as blockers.
- `WL-0MVWABT2Z001XMSD` (parent of the cross-repo feature) — discovery of
  sibling stores and foreign blocker resolution.
- `WL-0MVWEETA9006LFED` (**Cross-repo dependency documentation**) — the docs
  this fix must extend.
- `WL-0MM8V55PV1Q32K7D` (**Fix destructive `db.import()` in GitHub flows**) —
  introduced `upsertItems`; the same both-endpoints-local guard is the second
  drop point here.
- `SA-0MSC0BM1V0032UYT` — the merge-time prefix filter (defense-in-depth) being
  corrected.
- `WL-0MSAH26DD001XXST` — repo-context guard; unaffected, and must stay strict.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**A1 — Is this a genuine producer decision or a routine repo-search question?**

- Q: The item's root-cause pointer names only `src/sync/prefix-filter.ts`; is
  the import-store endpoint guard in scope?
- Answer (repo research, this intake): **Routine — in scope.** The ACs require a
  cross-repo edge to survive a "full sync round-trip" and a delta sync. A full
  `wl sync` runs the destructive `importWorkItems`, whose
  `getWorkItem(fromId) && getWorkItem(toId)` guard deletes any edge without a
  local foreign target. Therefore the import guard is a necessary part of
  satisfying the existing ACs, not new scope. Evidence:
  `packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts:227`,
  `src/commands/sync.ts:460`.
- Outcome: recorded as Root cause #2, a Key File and a test-plan item; no
  producer hold.

**A2 — Why did the reporter observe "re-adding and syncing again kept it"?**

- Q: The bug description says the loss is non-deterministic ("depends on whether
  the remote snapshot carries the edge"); what explains that?
- Answer (repo research): The merge is a union, and the persist step differs by
  sync kind. A **delta** persist uses `upsertItems` (non-destructive — it never
  deletes, so an existing foreign edge survives), while a **full** persist uses
  `importWorkItems` (destructive — it deletes any edge absent from
  `desiredEdges`). Whether a given sync is full or delta depends on the delta
  cadence/watermarks (`src/commands/sync.ts` export decision). Hence the loss
  is intermittent. Evidence: `src/sync/merge-collateral.ts`
  (`mergeDependencyEdges`), `import-export.ts:227` vs `:329`.
- Outcome: captured in Root cause; the fix must cover **both** persist kinds.

**A3 — Does "never resurrected after the local item deletes it" mean
`wl dep rm`, or deletion of the owning work item?**

- Q: AC3's "the local item deletes it" is ambiguous.
- Answer (reasonable assumption): interpret as **deletion of the local work item
  that owns the edge**, not `wl dep rm`. Rationale: `deleteWorkItem` already
  cascades `dependency_edges` (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:1356`),
  and the relaxed endpoint guard (keep iff *either* endpoint resolves) makes a
  deleted owner's edges unresolvable, so a stale remote snapshot cannot
  resurrect them. General `dep rm` resurrection on a stale remote snapshot is a
  **separate** pre-existing concern affecting all edges (not just cross-repo)
  and is out of scope here (scope-creep guard, Constraints) — logged as a
  follow-up if the implementer confirms it exists.
- Status: **assumption recorded, not a blocking question.**

**A4 — Does the "either endpoint" rule keep `foreign → local` edges too, even
though JSONL never exports them?**

- Q: The AC says "either endpoint"; AC text also says "dropping only edges whose
  local endpoint is itself foreign".
- Answer (reasonable assumption): the predicate is
  `allowedItemIds.has(fromId) || allowedItemIds.has(toId)` — keep if **any**
  endpoint is local. In practice remote edges are always `local → foreign`
  because `dependenciesFromEdges` only emits edges from exported (local) items,
  so the `foreign → local` branch is defensive only; it is harmless and matches
  the stated "either endpoint" intent. The redundant "local endpoint is itself
  foreign" phrasing is read as "neither endpoint is local → drop".
- Status: **assumption recorded, not a blocking question.**

**A5 — Duplicate-work check.**

- Command: `wl search` with keywords `cross-repo`, `foreign edge sync`,
  `dependency edge sync drop`, `dependency_edges import`.
- Answer: no completed item satisfies this item's ACs. Closest related items
  are `WL-0MVWEENZL008XGYC` (foreign edge CRUD — introduces the feature, does
  not fix sync) and `WL-0MM8V55PV1Q32K7D` (non-destructive `upsertItems` — a
  different guard). No duplicate; no rewrite needed.
